chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated it, saying: Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I was with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) at the time of the death of his son Abu Ja'far, and he had indicated to him and pointed him out. So I was thinking in myself and saying: This is the case of Abu Ibrahim and the case of Ismail. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: Yes, O Abu Hashim. God Almighty manifested (Bada) regarding Abu Ja'far and made Abu Muhammad take his place, just as God manifested regarding Ismail after Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had indicated him and appointed him. And it is as your soul narrated, even if the disbelievers dislike it. Abu Muhammad is my son, the successor after me; with him is what you need, and with him is the instrument of Imamate, and praise be to God.

key_terms.الْمُبْطِلُونَ: Al-Mubtilun (the disbelievers/those who deny the doctrine)
key_terms.بَدَا: Bada (divine manifestation or change of decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Bada in the death of Abu Ja'far and the succession of Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* elucidates the Shia doctrine of *Bada* by drawing a parallel between the death of Abu Ja'far (son of Imam al-Hadi) and the earlier death of Ismail (son of Imam al-Sadiq). It affirms that the shift in succession to Abu Muhammad (al-Hasan al-Askari) was a divine manifestation of will, ensuring the continuity of the Imamate despite the apparent loss of the designated heir. This narrative serves to validate the legitimacy of the final Imam against the claims of the *Mubtilun* (those who deny the Imamate after the death of the visible heir).
